analysis:
Examined the prompting-layer changes. ChatTemplateFixes.swift head 136-140 and ModelEOSPolicy.swift head 29-36 add stopStringScope, which returns the Harmony final-channel scope (GPTOSSHarmonyTemplateFixes.swift head 45-47) for GPT-OSS and nil otherwise. ReasoningStopScope.swift (new, 1-39) scopes client stop strings so they skip think, Gemma channel and tool-call spans for the qwen3, deepseekR1 and gemma4 parsers. These change only where stop strings match, not encryption, attestation or authorization.

GLM5NextResponseFormat.swift head 101 passes the new .logprobs event straight through while answer content is withheld. JSONAnswerFormat.swift head 81 ignores .logprobs when collecting content for validation.

Integration question (T-008/A-001 adjacency): if logprobs events carry token text from the withheld GLM JSON answer, streaming them before validation would expose content that withholding is meant to hold back. This is consumer-facing (the requester's own output), not cross-tenant, so it is not treated as a security regression. It does weaken the 'nothing unvalidated reaches the client' invariant at GLM5NextResponseFormat.swift head 83-84. Whether logprobs are emitted for GLM at all, and what they contain, must be checked in the MLXLMServer and CBv2 sources, which were not supplied.

The ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift unit was metadata only. Its file_changes entry shows .responseFormatCutOffByMaxTokens mapped to 422, consistent with existing handling.

Stop-scope parsing operates on model output in-process; an adversarial consumer can at most make generation run longer, which is still bounded by max_tokens. The CBv2StopStringScope implementation was not supplied: its opener/closer state machine and the handling of stops split across tokens need to be checked in integration. No change touches A-003, the TB-002 encryption path, T-041 cache salt, or TB-011.
